sections.bio:
𝐒𝐞𝐧𝐢𝐨𝐫 𝐒𝐨𝐟𝐭𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐄𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫 with 𝟏𝟎+ 𝐲𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐬 𝐨𝐟 𝐞𝐱𝐩𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐞𝐧𝐜𝐞 building and maintaining scalable web applications using .𝐍𝐄𝐓 technologies. Strong focus on 𝐛𝐚𝐜𝐤𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐝𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐥𝐨𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭, 𝐀𝐏𝐈 𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧, and designing clean, maintainable software architectures with 𝐀𝐒𝐏.𝐍𝐄𝐓 𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐞 and 𝐖𝐞𝐛 𝐀𝐏𝐈𝐬.

Experienced in designing robust software solutions, optimizing system performance, and collaborating with cross-functional teams to deliver reliable, production-ready applications. Skilled in building scalable systems with a focus on performance, maintainability, and long-term business value.

Currently open to 𝐫𝐞𝐦𝐨𝐭𝐞 𝐟𝐮𝐥𝐥-𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐨𝐩𝐩𝐨𝐫𝐭𝐮𝐧𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬, contract roles, and freelance projects where I can contribute to building modern .NET and AI-powered applications.

𝐂𝐨𝐫𝐞 𝐒𝐤𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐬 & 𝐓𝐞𝐜𝐡𝐧𝐨𝐥𝐨𝐠𝐢𝐞𝐬

𝐋𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐮𝐚𝐠𝐞𝐬 & 𝐅𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐞𝐰𝐨𝐫𝐤𝐬:
C#, .NET 8/9/10, ASP.NET Core, ASP.NET MVC, Web API

𝐀𝐫𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐫𝐞 & 𝐃𝐞𝐬𝐢𝐠𝐧 𝐏𝐚𝐭𝐭𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐬 & 𝐏𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐜𝐢𝐩𝐥𝐞𝐬:
RESTful APIs, Clean Architecture, Layered Architecture, Vertical Slice Architecture, Domain-Driven Design (DDD), CQRS, Repository Pattern, Mediator Pattern, OOP, SOLID, DRY, KISS, YAGNI & Clean Code

𝐃𝐚𝐭𝐚𝐛𝐚𝐬𝐞𝐬 & 𝐎𝐑𝐌:
SQL Server, Entity Framework Core, Dapper, LINQ, Stored Procedures

𝐂𝐥𝐨𝐮𝐝 & 𝐃𝐞𝐯𝐎𝐩𝐬:

𝐓𝐞𝐬𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠:
xUnit, Unit Testing, Integration Testing, Architecture Testing(NetArchTest.Rules), Fluent Assertions, Shouldly, NSubstitute

𝐎𝐛𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐯𝐚𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐭𝐲 & 𝐃𝐨𝐜𝐮𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧:
Swagger/OpenAPI, Scalar, API Versioning, Health Checks, Serilog

𝐅𝐫𝐨𝐧𝐭-𝐄𝐧𝐝:

𝐀𝐈 & 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐒𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦𝐬:
Generative AI, AI Agents, OpenAI Integration, AI Chatbot Development

𝐓𝐨𝐨𝐥𝐬:

💬 Let’s Connect

If you're looking for a software engineer who builds clean, scalable, and business-focused solutions - or if you're working on backend systems, cloud platforms, or AI-powered applications - I'd be happy to connect and explore potential collaboration opportunities.

posts.text:
𝐀 𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐥𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐦𝐲𝐬𝐞𝐥𝐟 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐨𝐭𝐡𝐞𝐫𝐬:
 
Rather than spending our time consuming content that is not permissible, let us pause and say 𝐀𝐥𝐡𝐚𝐦𝐝𝐮𝐥𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐡.
 
We should be grateful to Allah for protecting us from what may harm our faith and keeping us away from what is not permissible.
 
Not every opportunity we miss is a loss. Sometimes, being kept away from something is itself a blessing and a form of protection.
 
𝐌𝐚𝐲 𝐀𝐥𝐥𝐚𝐡 𝐠𝐮𝐢𝐝𝐞 𝐮𝐬, 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐮𝐬, 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐩 𝐮𝐬 𝐮𝐬𝐞 𝐨𝐮𝐫 𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞 𝐢𝐧 𝐰𝐚𝐲𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐚𝐭 𝐛𝐫𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐮𝐬 𝐜𝐥𝐨𝐬𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐨 𝐇𝐢𝐦. 𝐀𝐦𝐞𝐞𝐧. 🤲

One of the biggest challenges I’m facing as an indie developer from Bangladesh 🇧🇩 isn’t building the product.

It’s getting paid.

I recently found out that Dodo Payments doesn’t currently support businesses from Bangladesh.

For developers building SaaS and digital products, payment infrastructure is critical. We need solutions that support:

• Businesses registered in Bangladesh 🇧🇩
• International customers 🌍
• SaaS and digital products
• Easy and reliable payouts
• Simple integration for developers

It’s frustrating when you have a product ready to launch, but payment infrastructure becomes the blocker.

Hopefully, more global payment platforms will start supporting Bangladesh in the future.

If you’re a Bangladeshi founder/developer and have found a reliable payment solution for selling SaaS or digital products globally, I’d love to hear about your experience.

🚀 𝐀 𝐧𝐞𝐰 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐞𝐧 𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐛𝐁𝐢𝐝
 
𝐨𝐮𝐭𝐰𝐚𝐢𝐭.𝐥𝐨𝐥 is now listed in the 𝐅𝐫𝐞𝐞 section of ClimbBid.
 
It’s a simple way for indie hackers, founders, and developers to put their products in front of a new audience — without paying for a listing.
 
📌 Currently #3 on the leaderboard
 👆 Already receiving clicks
 🆓 Listed for free
 
Now we’ll see how far it can go through organic activity and discovery.
 
If you’re building a product, you can also list it on ClimbBid and see where it lands.
 
🔗 ClimbBid: climbbid.lol
 
#BuildInPublic #IndieHackers #SaaS #ProductLaunch #WebDevelopment

Launching a product is hard.

But getting people to discover it can be even harder.

That’s why I’m building 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐛𝐁𝐢𝐝.

The idea is simple:

🚀 You launch your product
→ Add it to ClimbBid
→ Founders & builders discover it
→ ClimbBid features interesting products
→ You share your feature
→ Your audience discovers ClimbBid
→ More founders join
→ More products get discovered

A simple loop where 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐡𝐞𝐥𝐩 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐧𝐨𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐞𝐝.

I’m building ClimbBid as an indie builder because I know how difficult it is to spend weeks or months building something — only to launch it and wonder:

“𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐝𝐨 𝐈 𝐚𝐜𝐭𝐮𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐩𝐞𝐨𝐩𝐥𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐬𝐞𝐞 𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐬?”

If you’re building a:

• SaaS
• Startup
• Developer tool
• Mobile or web app
• Side project
• AI product

👉 Check out 𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐦𝐛𝐁𝐢𝐝: https://climbbid.lol/

I’m starting small, but the goal is bigger:

𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐚 𝐠𝐞𝐧𝐮𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐥𝐲 𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐟𝐮𝐥 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐜𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐲 𝐩𝐥𝐚𝐭𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐦 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐢𝐞 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐞𝐫𝐬.

Build it.
Launch it.
Get discovered. 🚀

#ClimbBid #IndieHackers #BuildInPublic #SaaS #Startups #IndieBuilder #ProductDiscovery #Entrepreneurship

𝐁𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐨 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐭𝐚𝐮𝐠𝐡𝐭 𝐦𝐞 𝐬𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐈 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐬 𝐚 𝐬𝐨𝐟𝐭𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐞 𝐞𝐧𝐠𝐢𝐧𝐞𝐞𝐫.

For years, I focused on one thing:

𝐁𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝 𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭 𝐬𝐨𝐟𝐭𝐰𝐚𝐫𝐞.

As an engineer, that was the job.

But when you become a solo founder, the job changes completely.

You don't just build.

You also have to:

→ Find the problem
→ Build the product
→ Talk to customers
→ Market it
→ Create content
→ Learn distribution
→ Handle support
→ Make sales
→ Make difficult decisions
→ And keep going when nobody is paying attention.

And honestly, 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐤𝐞𝐭𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐡𝐚𝐬 𝐛𝐞𝐞𝐧 𝐨𝐧𝐞 𝐨𝐟 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐡𝐚𝐫𝐝𝐞𝐬𝐭 𝐩𝐚𝐫𝐭𝐬 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐦𝐞.

You can spend weeks building something you believe is valuable...

…and then realize almost nobody knows it exists.

That's been a humbling lesson.

I'm learning that building a product and getting people to care about it are two completely different skills.

𝐀 𝐠𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐭 𝐩𝐫𝐨𝐝𝐮𝐜𝐭 𝐝𝐨𝐞𝐬𝐧'𝐭 𝐚𝐮𝐭𝐨𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐢𝐜𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐟𝐢𝐧𝐝 𝐢𝐭𝐬 𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐫𝐬.

You have to learn how to tell the story.

You have to put yourself out there.

You have to accept rejection.

You have to keep experimenting.

And sometimes, you simply have to keep showing up.

I'm still figuring it out.

But I'm proud of the journey.

Because every difficult day is teaching me something I couldn't learn from a book, a course, or another person's success story.

My biggest lesson so far:

𝐃𝐨𝐧'𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐚𝐟𝐫𝐚𝐢𝐝 𝐭𝐨 𝐛𝐞 𝐛𝐚𝐝 𝐚𝐭 𝐬𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐲𝐨𝐮'𝐫𝐞 𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐫𝐧𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐟𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭 𝐭𝐢𝐦𝐞.

You don't need to be a great marketer on day one.

You just need to start.

Build → Share → Learn → Improve → Repeat.

That's the journey I'm choosing.

And I'm just getting started. 🚀

𝐈𝐟 𝐲𝐨𝐮'𝐫𝐞 𝐚𝐥𝐬𝐨 𝐛𝐮𝐢𝐥𝐝𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐬𝐨𝐦𝐞𝐭𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐠, 𝐞𝐬𝐩𝐞𝐜𝐢𝐚𝐥𝐥𝐲 𝐚𝐬 𝐚 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐨 𝐟𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐫, 𝐥𝐞𝐭'𝐬 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐧𝐞𝐜𝐭.

Let's share what we're learning, support each other, and grow together. 🤝
